subject.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue

question: Should aged lower-priority command-lane work be allowed to overtake fresh foreground work, or should this PR be narrowed to foreground-preserving aging that does not close the starvation issue?
rationale: Both policies are defensible, but they encode different user-facing scheduling guarantees and upgrade behavior; automation should not choose that product contract from a contradictory PR body and implementation.

options.title: Require contract alignment before merge
options.body: Pause merge until maintainers choose the starvation policy and the branch updates implementation, comments, tests, PR body, and proof to match it.

options.title: Sponsor true anti-starvation
options.body: Allow aged background/normal work to overtake fresh foreground after the threshold and require live or terminal proof of bounded low-priority wait under sustained foreground traffic.

options.title: Narrow to foreground-preserving aging
options.body: Keep one-tier aging only if the PR stops claiming to close steady-foreground starvation and links the remaining policy work to the canonical scheduler issue.

recommendation.title: Require contract alignment before merge
recommendation.body: Pause merge until maintainers choose the starvation policy and the branch updates implementation, comments, tests, PR body, and proof to match it.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest available history signal for original queue ownership and adjacent scheduler-policy work.
